classification.difficultyReason: Models triangles as unordered triples, expands the combination and identifies the integer giving the required consecutive-factor product.

content.prompt: A circle has $n$ evenly-spaced points on its circumference. Find the value of $n$ if there are 120 possible triangles that can be made.

answer.short:
$n=10$.

Each triangle is an unordered selection of three points, so $\binom{n}{3}=120$.
answer.worked: Any three distinct points on the circle determine a triangle. $$\begin{align*}\binom{n}{3}&=120\\\frac{n!}{3!(n-3)!}&=120\\\frac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{6}&=120\\n(n-1)(n-2)&=720.\end{align*}$$ Since $10\times9\times8=720$, $n=10$. For integers $n\geq3$, $n(n-1)(n-2)$ increases as $n$ increases, so this is the only possible value.
